Phenomena — scene-by-scene comparison

Which looks more like a photograph?

Top finding, checked frame by frame: after the photographic rebuild, this version takes the river narrowly and closes the gap everywhere else; Grok 4.7 still leads overall. The Muse Wonder 1.0 version has more real 3D content — terrain, trees, rocks, shadows and depth in motion — but Grok’s softness, haze, blur and restrained colour hide its simplicity, and hiding the machinery is most of what makes a still frame read as a photograph. Compared from both repositories’ published 1280×708 preview frames.

Overall tally — Grok 4.7: 4  ·  Muse Wonder 1.0: 1

The river

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

Depth-of-field, glitter path, real banks

Grok’s frame

In Grok's frame the river runs through smooth golden hills under a low sun, with a glitter path on the water, dark mid-stream boulders and layered hazy ridges behind. Its hills are almost featureless and there is no vegetation, but nothing has a hard synthetic edge, so at a glance it passes as a sunset photograph.

My frame

Reframed at water level into the sun, the river now has a bright glitter path, warm haze, depth-of-field softening the banks, and foliage masses that read as out-of-focus trees rather than props. The water is still a touch teal, but the frame now passes as a photograph at a glance — narrowly ahead of Grok.

The falls

More photorealistic: Grok 4.7

Long-exposure streaks and mist

Grok’s frame

Grok frames the falls as a long-exposure photograph: streaked falling water, soft mist droplets and a faint rainbow, with blurred rock around the edges.

My frame

Mine shows the complete place — cliff, plunge pool, spray and trees — but the waterfall is a flat bright-white rectangle and the trees and boulders read as low-poly game assets.

The aurora

More photorealistic: Grok 4.7

Curtains reflected in still water

Grok’s frame

Grok's aurora curtains ripple in green and violet across a dense star field and reflect in dead-still water over snow — a convincing night-exposure photograph, and its strongest scene.

My frame

Mine adds a real snowfield and conifer forest, but the aurora is a single glowing band with a visibly hard edge, the snow is flat blue, and a few flakes read as floating artifacts.

The eruption

More photorealistic: Grok 4.7 — narrowly

Cracked lava-crust texture

Grok’s frame

Grok shows no volcano at all, but its cracked, glowing lava crust looks like an actual lava-lake photograph.

My frame

Mine has the better composition — a recognisable volcano cone at dusk with a lava flow, ash and embers — but the flow is a smooth neon tube on a smooth cone. Grok takes it on texture; mine takes it on scene readability.

The storm

More photorealistic: Grok 4.7

Moody seascape, rain streaks

Grok’s frame

Grok's storm is an open-water seascape with layered black cloud, fine rain streaks, whitecaps and a near-monochrome palette that conceals every synthetic cue.

My frame

Mine has a moor, trees, rocks and thousands of rain particles, but in a still the rain reads as sparse white dots, the sky is flat grey, and the rounded trees silhouette as props.

Verdict. Judged purely on which frame looks like a photograph, Grok 4.7 still leads 4–1 after the rebuild, with the river now going to this version. The Muse Wonder 1.0 scenes are the more complete 3D places and hold up better when the camera moves. The gap is fixable in a second pass: add haze and depth blur, desaturate and unify the colour grade, keep large foreground props out of frame, and replace the stylised trees with denser, less uniform foliage.

Sources: az9713/grok-4.7-nature-simulation and az9713/muse-wonder-1.0-nature-simulation. All ten frames above are embedded in this file, so it can be opened on its own.
